new_results: If Y=M+sqrt(T)G with G standard Gaussian independent of (M,T) and E[T^(-1/2)]<=kappa, then every interval J of length L has probability <=2 Phi(kappa L/2)-1; the bound is sharp.
At kappa=sqrt(2*pi), every unit interval has mass <=0.7899085945560627, so every law in this class is at TV distance >=0.2100914054439373 from Uniform[0,1].
The fixed-kappa Gaussian-mixture class is not weakly dense in compactly supported probability laws; n-fold product TV distance from Uniform[0,1]^n is >=1-q_*^n.

Relaxing the inverse-scale budget to kappa changes the source determinant certificate to (I_k/(2*pi))*kappa^2*e_k(A^2)^(-1/(2k)); approximating Uniform[0,1] within TV eps forces kappa>=2 Phi^{-1}(1-eps/2), so this specific certificate diverges as eps->0.
Applying account04/B15 same-constant compiler to the Gaussian-mixture target interval bound gives p_Q in C_0 with height <=I_3<3, independently confirming regularity on that valid branch.
